questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian may be dangerous. Let them pass safely, then continue when it is safe.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It may be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving (such as vehicles striping, mowing, or removing snow). Work zones have orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: To avoid headlight glare at night, where should you look?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are bright, look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Let vehicles on your right pass only.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must let traffic already in the intersection pass. Be ready to stop, but you can continue if no other traffic is coming.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Fines for violations are the same as on regular roads.
You must slow down in work zones.
Only slow down if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Always reduce speed in work zones to stay safe. Driving carefully through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On vertical traffic signals, red is on top and green is on bottom. On horizontal signals, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when can you move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before moving back. Always check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the main road if you can.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?

options.text: Work zones.
Traffic rules.
School zones.
Directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped, orange with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. This sign means parking is not allowed here.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. On interstates, slower traffic must stay in the right lane. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on interstates. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Legal drugs—both prescription and over-the-counter—can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. The law against impaired driving applies to all drugs, not just illegal ones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated the same as a yield sign.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossbuck sign is a yield sign. You must yield to trains and railroad equipment.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra space when stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially when rain just starts. Your tires sit on a layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down and increase your stopping distance.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can be deadly.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can be deadly."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can be deadly."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of fatal crashes. Above 80 mph, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because it can cause other drivers to make risky passing moves.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line allows passing. A solid yellow line does not. Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.

questions.question: When parallel parking, park within ____ of the curb.

options.text: 10 inches
12 inches
18 inches
24 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches
questions.explanation: Park with your wheels parallel to the curb and within 12 inches of it. Park only where you will not block traffic and where other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: In fog, a driver should turn on high beam headlights to see better.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights. Do not use high beams in fog.

questions.question: When may you text while driving?

options.text: If you can text without looking at your phone.
Never.
If you use a voice-to-text feature.
If you only look away from the road for a moment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is illegal in Rhode Island. Using a cell phone while driving is a major distraction.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Some crossings do not have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down and let other vehicles or pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all four corners, when should you yield the right-of-way?

options.text: To the driver on your left.
To the driver who arrived first.
To the driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go through in the order they arrived. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the left must yield to the one on the right.

questions.question: Why should you be extra careful around motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians even though they were looking. These are smaller and harder to spot than cars. Stay alert for them on the road.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot pass other vehicles here.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass. When a solid yellow line is next to your lane, you cannot pass.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause hearing loss.
It causes pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It reduces engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to make sure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Press the brakes gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work better with low beams.
